question.text: A stationary source is emitting sound at a fixed frequency <math> <mrow> <msub> <mi>f</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> </mrow> </math>, which is reflected by two cars approaching the source. The difference between the frequencies of sound reflected from the cars is <math> <mrow> <mn>1.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow> </math> of <math> <mrow> <msub> <mi>f</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> </mrow> </math>. What is the difference in the speeds of the cars (in <math> <mrow> <mtext>km</mtext></mrow> </math> per hour) to the nearest integer ? The cars are moving at constant speeds much smaller than the speed of sound which is <math> <mrow> <mn>330</mn><mtext> </mtext><msup> <mrow> <mtext>ms</mtext></mrow> <mrow> <mtext>-1</mtext></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math>.

solution.text:
Let v1 and v2 be the velocities of sources, then apparent frequencies are

f1=c+v1c-v1f0 and f2=c+v2c-v2f0

Then difference between frequencies is,

∆f=2∆vCf0 ∵ c>>v1 & c>>v2 

∴∆v=7 kmph.
